newsitem.title: FINLAND: Tampella sees higher 1997 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Tampella sees higher 1997 net profit.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Tampella Oy said on Friday it expected its 1997 profit before extraordinary items and tax to be at least on par with last year, but the net profit would be higher.
"The 1997 earnings before extraordinary items, appropriations and taxes are expected to remain at least at the level of 1996," Tampella said in a statement with its 1996 results.
"The net result is expected to be better," Tampella said, referring to lower taxes and minorities.

Last year, Tampella's earnings improved by about 330 million markka; to a 141 million markka profit before extraordinary items and tax from a 188 million markka loss. The group's comparable net sales rose 14 percent to 4.52 billion markka.
Tampella said its orderbooks were good but unevenly distributed at end-1996.
Expectations for economic growth worldwide were quite positive although the German economy still looked weak, it said.
"On the whole, the price level of base metals is slightly lower than a year ago. On average, prices are expected to remain at current levels," Tampella said.

Referring to its Tamrock business group, Tampella said demand for hard rock mining equipment was lively in Africa, Australia and South America while prospect in Canada and western Europe had weakened.
Demand for coal mining equipment was good in Australia, but Tampella said that overall, it did not expect demand to grow.

Net sales of the Roxon business group, a maker of bulk handling equipment, would rise this year, mainly as a result of the acquisition last year of Austrian Voest-Alpine Bergtechnik (VAB), Tampella said.
